key_insight: Compared with conventional APS, axial-feed supersonic HV-APS produced denser, harder Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings with 27% lower sliding wear volume, but nearly unchanged erosion resistance at 90° impact.
engineering_relevance: HV-APS is promising for Cr₃C₂–NiCr-coated steel components exposed to sliding wear, though its benefits should not be assumed for normal-impact erosion.
method: Sprayed Metco 5241 Cr₃C₂–NiCr powder onto S235 steel using radial-feed APS and axial-feed HV-APS.
Compared microstructure, phase transformations, porosity, and microhardness.
Evaluated erosion at 90° impact and ball-on-disc sliding wear under a 30 N load.
evidence_signal: HV-APS versus APS yielded 6.16% versus 11.99% porosity, 1141 versus 897 HV0.2 hardness, and 2.85 versus 3.90 mm³ wear volume, while specific erosion rates remained close at 0.19 versus 0.20 mg/g.
watch_item: The comparison changes both torch technology and powder-feed geometry, so the improvements cannot be attributed to axial feeding alone.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
